products.summary: Medium 16:9 pen tablet with two pens and the Quick Keys dial remote in one box. The active area maps edge to edge onto a widescreen monitor, and the dial handles brush size, zoom and Lightroom sliders.
products.fit: Photographers and retouchers editing on a 24 to 32 in monitor who want a dial and shortcut keys without paying Wacom Intuos Pro money.
caveats: Wireless uses a USB dongle that needs a free USB-A port (adapter included), not Bluetooth.
The tablet itself has only 3 buttons; the 8 keys and dial live on the separate Quick Keys remote.
Several reviewers hit a Quick Keys dial that stopped responding in Photoshop or needed a driver reinstall; the driver also conflicts with an installed Wacom driver.
No touch input; plan to keep a mouse or trackpad for scrolling.
The v2 bundle sells for more and adds v2 pens and HP Anyware support only; the original bundle is the better buy for photo editing.

notes: Query choice: 'best drawing tablet for photo editing' (variants also autocomplete). Current answers are PetaPixel (blocked, could not read), XPPen's own blog, and generic affiliate roundups. Xencelabs Medium Bundle is widely named the Intuos Pro alternative for photographers (DIYPhotography, KelbyOne, Fstoppers), so it honestly wins the main desk-monitor segment on area/pens/dial/price; Wacom Intuos Pro Medium 2025 honestly wins the 'all controls on the tablet + Bluetooth' segment and is named as such in the lead. Pain points counted: no Bluetooth / dongle takes a USB-A port (3: Fstoppers 2022, Creative Bloq Small review, AppleInsider); only 3 tablet buttons (3: Parkablogs, Creative Bloq, AppleInsider); Quick Keys dial or wireless glitches (3: DIYPhotography, Yanko Design, Fstoppers commenter); Xencelabs driver conflicts with Wacom driver (2: PetaPixel 2021, Parkablogs comment); Wacom Intuos Pro 2025 touch removed (3: Wacom support page, PhotoshopCafe, r/wacom via snippet) plus 4 forum posts on Bluetooth/Mac wake/Sequoia driver/cursor glitch; small tablet struggles with large or dual monitors (2, Lightroom Queen); tablet optional for Lightroom (3 of 6 in same thread). Verified today on xencelabs.com/us (not Shopify; read via WebFetch): Medium Bundle $264.00 (list $329.99), Medium $224.99 (list $249.99), Small $59.99 (list $139.99), Quick Keys alone $79.99, Medium Bundle v2 $329.99 (page showed no strikethrough; store grid showed $263.99 for v2, inconsistent, so v2 was not recorded). Store shows Add to Cart on all three; no explicit stock text. Return policy and 24-month warranty read on the store. Site banner 'Buy 2 get 20% off, buy 3 get 30% off' is a cart promo, not a code; WELCOME5 is from the sign-up popup. Amazon: amzcheck.py returned blocked:true for every search and ASIN, so no Amazon ASINs or price comparison could be done; no Amazon records were created. Not verified today and kept off the page or dated: Wacom estore (403 on every URL) so the Intuos Pro Medium price is given only as the February 2025 launch list price $379.95 from CG Channel coverage; Wacom Intuos Medium Bluetooth price not verified (no number printed); Huion Inspiroy 2 M US price unreadable (store JSON empty) so that row was dropped; XPPen Deco Pro Gen 2 store page shows a single $159.99 price for the listing with MW as the base size, printed with date.
